data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaves attached at the same node along the rachis in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are regularly spaced along the rachis, not clustered at the tip)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the structure is a leaflet-bearing axis, a rachis, with multiple leaflets attached, confirming it is a compound leaf)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (the rachis terminates in a single terminal leaflet, as seen clearly in the first and fourth images)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (one terminal leaflet plus three pairs of lateral leaflets are clearly visible on the main leaf structure in the first and fourth images)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (the lateral leaflets are attached at different heights along the rachis, not in a strict opposite pair, as seen in the close-up images)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaflet margins are smooth and undulating, lacking any teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are elongated with the widest point near the base and tapering towards the apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaflets taper to a distinct, elongated point at the tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaflets taper towards the base where they attach to the rachis)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a single midrib runs the length of the leaflet with smaller veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, pinnate, branching at an angle from the midrib
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaflets have a distinct glossy sheen reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (the surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (the rachis, which functions as the extension of the petiole for the leaflets, is elongated)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the rachis appears round in cross-section, lacking wings or grooves)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the visible stems are thin and green, typical of a young seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stems appear smooth)
    19. Stem color: brownish-green (the main stem is greenish, turning brownish where it is older or dried)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the base of the leaflets or leaf)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The leaflets exhibit a distinct wavy or undulating margin. Some leaflets show minor damage in the form of small holes. The plant is growing amidst a bed of dry leaf litter.
